name: Thulium
occurrence: The rarest naturally occurring lanthanide (excluding radioactive promethium), found in trace amounts in monazite ore.
majorUses: Portable X-ray devices (thulium-170 isotope, doesn't require mains power)
notableCharacteristics: Named after 'Thule', an ancient, semi-mythical name for a land in the far north, continuing the Scandinavian naming pattern of the rare earths.
whyHere: Its thirteen 4f electrons, just one short of a completely filled subshell, give thulium compounds distinctive optical absorption used in solid-state lasers, though its extreme rarity limits large-scale industrial use.
didYouKnow: A thulium-170 based portable X-ray unit can be carried into the field and doesn't need an electrical power source to generate X-rays, unlike a conventional X-ray machine — useful for remote or battlefield medicine.
genZNote: The rarest lanthanide that still ends up in portable X-ray machines. Scarce but doing real work.
